verdicts.title: Zero Excess and Minimal Length in Finite Coxeter Groups
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Let $\mathcal{W}$ be the set of strongly real elements of $W$, a Coxeter group. Then for $w \in \mathcal{W}$, $e(w)$, the excess of $w$, is defined by $e(w) = \min\{\ell(x) + \ell(y) - \ell(w) \; | \; w=xy, x^2 = y^2 = 1\}$. When $W$ is finite we may also define $E(w)$, the reflection excess of $w$. The main result established here is that if $W$ is finite and $X$ is a $W$-conjugacy class, then there exists $w \in X$ such that $w$ has minimal length in $X$ and $e(w) = 0 = E(w)$.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract of the cited paper discusses properties of strongly real elements in Coxeter groups, specifically their excess and reflection excess. This is orthogonal to the conjecture under review which relates the number of non-isomorphic Coxeter groups generated by transpositions of Boolean functions to the pseudorandomness of those functions.

verdicts.title: The Dynkin diagram cohomology of finite Coxeter groups
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Let D be a connected graph. The Dynkin complex CD(A) of a D-algebra A was introduced by the second author in [TL2] to control the deformations of quasi-Coxeter algebra structures on A. In the present paper, we study the cohomology of this complex when A is the group algebra of a Coxeter group W and D is the Dynkin diagram of W.
